_schema.purpose: Concrete situations to run through the engine. The point is not that the engine invents workflows, but that when a real need is expressed the engine proposes a composition whose join keys, mode and side-effect profile survive inspection.

fields.need: the situation in one sentence, as a person would say it
fields.chain: the connectors the composition must touch, in intended order
fields.expected_pattern: one of the nine patterns in composition.md
fields.forbid: side-effect levels that must not appear anywhere in the chain, or []
fields.expect_mode: the strongest mode the engine should find for the weakest hop: direct | inferred | any

_schema.origin: 20 generic, 20 drawn from Jani's context (ABM research, the HCMC AI reseller funnel, women-heavy market research)

Take the leads I pulled from a prospecting database and start an outbound sequence.
Enrich the companies in my CRM with firmographic data.
Reconcile my storefront orders against my accounting ledger.
Get payment records into the books without retyping them.
Turn survey responses into a queryable table.
Put my warehouse data in front of the team as a dashboard.
Check whether any of my CRM contacts turned up in a breach.
Turn what was said in my meetings into tasks I will actually do.
Make the emails that need action show up on my task list.
Publish an analysis as a shareable page instead of losing it in chat.
Take a signed contract and file it where the team can find it.
Get my ad and site metrics into one place I can query.
Turn a research question into sourced reading I can cite.
Track shipments against the orders that produced them.
Turn customer support volume into something I can chart over time.
Build a deck from numbers rather than rebuilding it by hand each month.
Watch for errors in production and page a human when it matters.
Turn candidate applications into a reviewable pipeline.
Keep a durable record linking records across two systems so re-runs do not duplicate.
Find mid-market Western companies that look like they need AI help, and get them into a CRM.
Enrich those companies with headcount and hiring signals before I decide who to contact.
Find the actual decision-maker's email at a company I have only a domain for.
Run cold outreach to a qualified list without sending anything I have not seen.
Track which outreach threads got a reply so I can follow up on the live ones.
Turn a discovery call into a written brief the HCMC provider can quote against.
Give a prospect a credible landing page for the offer without building a site.
Let a prospect book a call at a time that works, without me chasing.
Invoice a Western client from Vietnam and have it land in the books.
Send the onboarding paperwork for signature and keep the executed copy.
Keep every prospect interaction in one durable store instead of my memory.
Check a target market's economic conditions before I pitch into it.
Compare how Claude is actually used in a country against where I am selling.
Turn my research notes into a paper I can hand a client.
Find which industries employ mostly women in a given country, from public data.
Pull public health and demographic series for a region I am researching.
Find software categories women-heavy businesses actually review and rate.
Check whether a market I am researching has real procurement money in it.
Keep the whole research corpus searchable without re-reading everything.
Produce a weekly brief from calendar, inbox and the task list.
